title: Grade 4 Science — Mon, Jun 16
description: Skeletal System — Day 1 of 5: Bones — structure and functions
subject: science

questions.question: The skeletal system is made up of:
options: All the bones in the body
questions.explanation: The skeletal system consists of all the bones in the body. The human adult body has 206 bones.

questions.question: How many bones does an adult human body have?
questions.explanation: An adult human body has 206 bones. Babies are born with about 270–300 bones that fuse as they grow.

questions.question: The study of bones is called:
questions.explanation: Osteology is the scientific study of bones. Osteo = bone (Greek).

questions.question: The main function of the skeleton is to:
options: Support the body, protect organs, and help movement
questions.explanation: The skeleton has three main functions: (1) support — gives the body shape; (2) protection — shields organs; (3) movement — muscles pull on bones.

questions.question: Which organ does the skull (cranium) protect?
questions.explanation: The skull (cranium) surrounds and protects the brain. Without the skull, the brain would be vulnerable to injury.

questions.question: Which bones protect the heart and lungs?
questions.explanation: The ribcage — 12 pairs of ribs and the sternum (breastbone) — forms a protective cage around the heart and lungs.

questions.question: The vertebral column (spine/backbone) protects:
questions.explanation: The vertebral column (spine) surrounds and protects the spinal cord — the main nerve highway of the body.

questions.question: Bones are made mainly of:
options: Calcium and phosphorus (making them hard and strong)
questions.explanation: Bones are made primarily of calcium and phosphorus, which make them hard. Milk, yogurt, and leafy vegetables supply calcium for strong bones.

questions.question: The soft, jelly-like substance inside large bones that produces blood cells is called:
questions.explanation: Bone marrow is found inside large bones (like the femur). Red bone marrow produces red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

questions.question: Which of these foods helps build strong bones?
questions.explanation: Milk, cheese, yogurt, and green leafy vegetables are rich in calcium — essential for strong bones.

questions.question: Cartilage is:
options: Flexible connective tissue found at joint ends and in the nose and ears
questions.explanation: Cartilage is softer and more flexible than bone. It covers the ends of bones at joints to reduce friction, and forms your nose and ears.

questions.question: Why do babies have more bones than adults?
options: Many small bones fuse together as the body grows
questions.explanation: Babies start with about 270–300 bones, many of which are cartilage. As they grow, bones harden (ossify) and small bones fuse, resulting in 206 bones in adults.

questions.question: The smallest bone in the human body is found in the:
questions.explanation: The stapes (stirrup) in the middle ear is the smallest bone in the human body — only about 3 mm long.

questions.question: The largest bone in the human body is the:
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the body.

questions.question: Without a skeleton, the human body would:
options: Collapse — it would have no support or shape
questions.explanation: Without bones, the body would have no support — it would be a shapeless mass like a jellyfish. The skeleton is the body's framework.
